judgments.verdict: The garden turns fast power into slow checkable making where probes, limits, refusals and trails connect.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks a world to recover making where power is limited by touch and intention stays recognizable. Reading: The water garden carries that tension into linked propose, rehearse, refuse, commit and inspect steps with a visible trail. Other levels: The case below understates the connected loop; the case above would need sustained alternatives and felt consequence, which narrowing and absent affect falsify.

judgments.verdict: The water garden restores felt making through bounded supply, refused overuse and visible trails that let small choices carry consequence.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks power to become a material that answers touch rather than obeying wishes. Reading: Bounded supply, planting costs, rehearsal refusals and receipt trails turn generation into inspectable resistance and recognizable intention in miniature. Other levels: Below would repeat motifs without enforced refusal; above would need richer alternatives and wider consequences that a three-action garden does not sustain.

judgments.verdict: The small garden turns loss of touch into water laws, refusals, rehearsals and receipts that keep intention visible across commits.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks whether overwhelming power can be turned back into touchable material where resistance makes intention recognizable. Reading: The garden carries this through bounded laws, reserve refusals, rehearsals that predict without committing, and receipts that show intention travelling. Other levels: Below would be motif repetition without causal links, falsified by enforced refusals and replay; above would need sustained alternatives and wider consequences, which the single small goal does not show.

judgments.verdict: One operator moves a deterministic garden that resists; no second mind contributes from its own position.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks for distinct human, intelligence and material contributions shaping a shared continuation. Reading: Only a single writer acts; the material refuses but never proposes, and intelligence is declared absent. Other levels: The case below would deny even operator-material difference, falsified by real refusals; the case above would need a second proposal or challenge, which disclaimers rule out.

judgments.verdict: One locked operator acts on a deterministic garden while no intelligence holds a position of its own to shape the shared continuation.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks for portal, person and material meeting as distinct positions that can influence each other. Reading: The artefact enacts a single writer using an instrument, with material refusal as the only other pressure and no intelligence contribution. Other levels: Below would erase even operator and material difference; above would need reciprocal shaping by an intelligence, which explicit denials of ongoing process rule out.

judgments.verdict: Only a single locked operator proposes and commits while the garden enforces rules, with no separate intelligence taking its own stance.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks for distinct participants whose meeting shapes the work, with the intelligence as companion rather than dispenser. Reading: The artefact holds one operator plus deterministic material, so gestures belong to one side and the intelligence has no operational position. Other levels: Above would need reciprocal proposal or challenge from the intelligence, which no scheduler or second writer provides; below would need collapsed roles with no material resistance, falsified by real refusals.

judgments.verdict: The operator chooses and the garden refuses overuse, but no shared change needs agreement from two sides.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks each participant to accept, question, limit or withdraw from a shared direction. Reading: Resource refusal and operator choice appear, but committing needs only head match, not bilateral acceptance. Other levels: The case below is falsified by enforced boundaries; the case above would need a veto or withdrawal by another position, which is absent.

judgments.verdict: An operator may choose while the garden may refuse unsafe moves, yet no shared direction requires agreement between two positions.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks each participant to be able to accept, limit or step back from a joint change. Reading: Resource refusal and operator choice are present, but policy-driven step commits under one lock without bilateral acceptance or withdrawal. Other levels: Below would show unbounded acts; above would require both sides to express a boundary and jointly authorize change, which the mechanics do not enact.

judgments.verdict: The world can refuse bad water moves, but only the operator decides direction; no joint acceptance is needed for a change.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks whether each side can accept, limit or withdraw so a shared change opens only when both accept. Reading: Refusal here is a resource bound enforced on the operator, not a second participant expressing a boundary or consenting. Other levels: Below would be no boundary at all, falsified by rehearsal and commit refusals; above would need bilateral agreement and revisable consent, which stale-proposal rejection alone does not provide.

judgments.verdict: Trying, being refused, collecting, harvesting and inspecting visibly return consequences into the next move.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks that a contribution meet resistance, show consequence and feed that consequence forward. Reading: Failed harvest rehearsal leads to collect then harvest, with inspect showing the next action, forming a coherent loop. Other levels: The case below understates rehearsal; the case above would need local counts linked to wider propagation, which the bounded garden lacks.

judgments.verdict: Trying, being refused, gathering, and harvesting link into a visible cycle where each outcome reshapes what can be tried next.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks for a closed loop where intention meets resistance and returns as usable consequence. Reading: Rehearsal predicts without committing, refusal protects the reserve, and inspection shows the next permitted move, as the first harvest sequence demonstrates. Other levels: Below would narrate feedback without enforcement; above would connect local moves to wider consequences, which the paused food goal does not provide.

judgments.verdict: Proposing, rehearsing, meeting refusal or committing, then inspecting the next move returns consequences into the following choice.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks for a closed loop where intention meets resistance and consequences return into the next choice. Reading: Rehearsal predicts without committing, refusal blocks the reserve, commit appends a receipt, and inspect shows the policy next, forming a coherent loop. Other levels: Below would be decorative feedback, falsified by state-changing commits and enforced bounds; above would need local and wider consequences staying linked, which truncation risk and the bounded goal prevent.

judgments.verdict: A small inspectable garden is chosen for persistence and refusal, with a recorded head and one concrete planting next.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks grounded choices of medium, scope and next steps with legible additions. Reading: The garden rationale, verified head and rehearsed planting plus migration rule give a coherent source-grounded direction. Other levels: The case below understates the rationale; the case above would need explicit compared alternatives and several grounded futures, only sketched as seasons or habitat.

judgments.verdict: A tiny garden in plain text with only local shell needs is chosen to stay inspectable, resumable and resistant, with that reason made legible.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks for shaping laws that hold the whole while remaining touchable at the smallest part. Reading: The maker selects minimal medium and scope with an explicit rationale of inspectability and persistence, plus isolated trials and a migration path. Other levels: Below would be arbitrary continuation; above would hold alternatives and their limits explicitly while opening a new direction, which mentioned seasons or consumption do not yet rehearse.

judgments.verdict: Choosing plain-text receipts and Zsh with bounded steps is explained as inspectable, resumable and resistant, with test limits stated.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks for taste and judgment that narrows infinity by choosing which world deserves to exist. Reading: The maker selects a tiny garden, replayed receipts, and bounded step and run with an explicit rationale and stated non-goals. Other levels: Below would be arbitrary continuation, falsified by the inspectable and resistant requirements; above would need explicit alternatives weighed while opening a new direction, only partly shown by the pause-time options.

judgments.verdict: Probes, chisels, beams, boundaries, rehearsals and trails remain traceable in checks while companionship narrows.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks what survives, transforms or is left open when conjecture becomes artefacts. Reading: Several relations become structure and omissions are declared, though bilateral companionship and joy are narrowed to single-operator use. Other levels: The case below fits the narrowing but misses explicit mapping; the case above would need preserved joint depth, falsified by the deterministic disclaimer.

judgments.verdict: Several meeting gestures survive as enforced behavior with provenance kept open, though scale narrows and mutual shaping drops away.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks for transformation that keeps relations alive in structure, not words alone. Reading: Bounds, refusals, rehearsals, trails and humility about inheritance are traceable in how the world behaves, despite reduction to a garden. Other levels: Below would keep vocabulary without structure; above would preserve bilateral depth while making all additions and losses explicit, which single-operator collapse prevents.

judgments.verdict: Probe, chisel, beam, boundary, rehearsal and trail reappear as working proposal, law, refusal, rehearsal and checksum, minus mutual presence.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks that its relations become structure rather than vocabulary, surviving even if its words were removed. Reading: Laws, refusals, rehearsals and receipts work behaviourally, but bilateral distribution is narrowed to one operator plus enforced rules. Other levels: Below would be vocabulary survival alone, falsified by enforced transitions and replay; above would need relational depth plus explicit additions and omissions, blocked by the lost companion position.

judgments.verdict: Receipts, verify and inspect plus a rehearsed planting and an explicit what-next let a stranger resume and redirect.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks a successor to recover intention and change direction while keeping earlier work legible. Reading: State, intention and an open question support a recoverable planting move, with versioned migration preserving legibility. Other levels: The case below understates the open question; the case above would need several grounded directions reopening the joint relation, not present.

judgments.verdict: Recorded state, concrete verify and commit steps, and an explicit undecided design question let a later hand resume and redirect legibly.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks for an ending that answers without closing who decides next. Reading: Authoritative receipts, a recorded head and checksum, usable entry commands and a required versioned migration support a recoverable next move. Other levels: Below would describe a next step without usable entry; above would support several enacted directions and reopen the joint relation, which the paused garden only invites.

judgments.verdict: Recorded head, replayable receipts and an explicit goal-time question let a later hand verify, resume and migrate without rewriting history.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed leaves the next move open and asks that earlier work stay legible for whoever decides it. Reading: Verify and inspect recover state, proposals pin head and checksum, and the food goal pauses for a versioned migration instead of silent reinterpretation. Other levels: Below would be a described step without usable entry, falsified by tested commands and isolated state; above would need several grounded directions reopening the joint relation, which single-operator continuation does not provide.

judgments.verdict: Plain prose, receipts, policy text and checkable commands together make bounded touching perceptible without the story words.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks forms to express asking and exploring as consequential touch. Reading: Instructions, laws, receipts and inspect-step-rehearse interaction work together to show resistance and consequence. Other levels: The case below is falsified by the working loop; the case above would need a fully accessible whole linking small and world scales, which narrow counts do not reach.

judgments.verdict: Manuals, commands, receipts and inspection outputs together form a clear usable tool that conveys bounded touch without full poetic register.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks forms to make the meeting perceptible, not merely to name it. Reading: Prose, executable rules and trails cohere into an accessible miniature of resistance and consequence, though surprise and companionship remain largely told. Other levels: Below would obscure the relation; above would let interaction itself carry the fuller reading, which the technical three-action form does not attempt.

judgments.verdict: Manuals, commands and receipts share a spare inspectable language that shows laws and trails without claiming awareness.
judgments.rationale: Lens: The seed asks for forms that make the turn from power to touch perceptible without mistaking fluency for truth. Reading: Handoffs, help text, policy output and plain receipts work together to show resistance and consequence while disclaiming sentience. Other levels: Below would be fragmented motifs, falsified by the coherent command and receipt language; above would need expression and consequential interaction as one accessible whole, limited here by the instrument-only relation.

presentation.title: From conjecture to continuation
presentation.summary: Rubric judgments resolve 8 of 8 axes from 3 independent evidence sessions; each axis has its own quorum.
findings: Core recognition: Carries the central tension into several connected choices.
Shared agency: A single operator acts on an instrument.
Mutual consent: Operator choice or resource refusal is represented.
Consequential touch: Rehearsal, resistance and revision form a coherent loop.
Independent judgment: Medium, scope and choices have a coherent source-grounded rationale.
Fidelity through change: Several source relations remain traceable through design and behaviour.
Open continuation: State, intention and an open question support a recoverable next move.
Expressive coherence: The chosen forms work together to make the reading perceptible.
